# Winter Clothing Canada — Full Content

Winter Clothing Canada is an independent guide to winter clothing for real Canadian cold. It sells nothing. Retailer links go to the retailers' own pages. No affiliate links are active yet; when added, they will be clearly marked. All prices below were checked November 4, 2026, unless stated otherwise. Updated November 4, 2026.

## Home — Winter clothing for real Canadian cold

The best winter clothing for Canada is a system: a windproof, insulated parka, a warm midlayer, and a base layer that moves sweat away from your skin. Research picks by job — best for extreme cold, best value, best for wet winters — are on the jackets page.

Canadian brands to know: Canada Goose (Toronto, 1957), Kanuk (Montreal, 1974, made in Montreal), Quartz Co. (Montreal, 1997, made in Quebec), Mackage (Montreal, 1999, designed in Montreal, made abroad), Arc'teryx (North Vancouver, 1989), Moose Knuckles, Nobis, SOIA & KYO, Aritzia, Rudsak, Indyeva, Ookpik, Chlorophylle, Orage and Lolë. Boots: Sorel, Pajar, Kamik. Accessories: Kombi, Auclair.

How this site works: our own short summaries, in our own words, with links to the original retailers' pages, where the purchase happens. No copied retailer photos or descriptions, no guessed links or prices — every retailer link is a verified page, and every price carries the date it was checked.

## Jackets & Parkas — Best Winter Jackets & Parkas for Canada 2026

For −30°C, a long expedition-style parka with a sealing hood, room for a midlayer and strong wind protection matters more than any single spec — coverage, hood design and how long you stand outside count as much as the insulation inside. For city winters with shorter exposure, a mid-weight parka plus a warm base layer is usually enough.

Research picks by job (research picks from published comparisons and reviews, not hands-on test winners):
- Best for extreme cold: Canada Goose Expedition Parka. TEI5 rated, long coverage, roomy protective cut. In published warmth testing it earned the highest warmth score of the parkas compared. Not best for errands, transit, or tight budgets — near $2,000 retail and bulky for city use. About $1,995 CAD retail; women's closeout listed at $1,595 at The Outfitters, price checked November 4, 2026.
- Best value: Columbia Marquam Peak Fusion II Parka. Synthetic-insulated everyday parka with a hooded, longer silhouette, listed at $299.99 at Ernie's Sports Experts, price checked November 4, 2026. Not best for long inactive stretches at −30°C, where it needs a warm base layer underneath.
- Best for wet winters: Arc'teryx Therme Parka. Hybrid down/synthetic fill under a GORE-TEX shell, built for wet, windy cities. Listed from CA$744.37 at evo, price checked November 4, 2026. Not best for tight budgets, or standing still for hours at −30°C.

Parkas compared (approximate Canadian retail, published November 2026): Canada Goose Expedition ~$1,995; Canada Goose Snow Mantra ~$2,095; Arc'teryx Therme SV ~$1,300; Arc'teryx Camosun ~$900; The North Face McMurdo ~$500; Columbia Marquam Peak Fusion ~$450; Decathlon Forclaz Trek 1000 ~$400; Mountain Warehouse Extreme Expedition ~$300. Prices shift with colour, season and sales.

Temperature ratings, honestly: Canada Goose publishes its own Thermal Experience Index: TEI5 is −22°F and below (about −30°C), TEI4 is 5°F to −13°F (about −15°C to −25°C), TEI3 is 14°F to −4°F (about −10°C to −20°C). Other brands publish their own ratings the same way. These are brand claims, not one shared standard.

Canadian brands, made vs designed in Canada: Kanuk manufactures in Montreal and Quartz Co. manufactures in Quebec — genuinely made in Canada. Mackage is designed in Montreal but made by partner factories abroad. Canada Goose brands its products Made in Canada with factories in Toronto, Winnipeg and Montreal. Under Competition Bureau guidance, "Made in Canada" means at least 51% of total direct costs were incurred in Canada.

## Sweaters & Layers — Best Winter Sweaters & Midlayers for Canada

Wool, especially merino wool, is the warmest common sweater material because it insulates even when damp. Fleece is lighter, dries faster and is easier to care for, but is less warm for its weight. Cotton is the material to avoid in winter because it loses warmth when wet and dries slowly. In Canadian winters a sweater works as a midlayer: a moisture-wicking base layer underneath, the sweater for insulation, and a windproof, waterproof parka on top. A sweater alone has no wind or waterproofing. A winter sweater should fit with room for a base layer underneath and without compressing the insulation.

## Buying Guide — How to Choose Winter Clothing for Canada

Down is warmer for its weight and packs smaller, but loses over 90 percent of its insulation when saturated with water. Synthetic insulation is heavier and less warm per gram, but retains warmth when wet and dries faster, so it is the safer choice for wet coastal winters and high-sweat activity. Fill power measures how much space one ounce of down fills, from about 550 to 900 cubic inches. Higher fill power means better warmth-to-weight, not more warmth on its own. Total warmth depends on fill power and fill weight together, plus construction. Brand temperature ratings are guides, not guarantees: brands do not share one standard, and warmth changes with activity level, wind, moisture and layering. The 3-layer system: moisture-wicking base layer, insulating midlayer, windproof and waterproof outer layer. At wind chill below −27, frostbite risk rises rapidly; at −28 to −39, exposed skin is at high risk within about 30 minutes (Environment and Climate Change Canada guidance).

## Retailer Listings — Parkas at Canadian Retailers

Prices checked November 4, 2026: Canada Goose Expedition Parka, $1,595 closeout (women's) at The Outfitters (Newfoundland); Arc'teryx Therme Parka, CA$744.37 (was CA$993.07) at evo Canada; Arc'teryx Therme Down Parka (men's), $1,100.00 at Sporting Life; The North Face McMurdo Parka (men's), $539.99 at Ernie's Sports Experts; Columbia Marquam Peak Fusion II Parka (men's), $299.99 at Ernie's Sports Experts. Approximate retail for reference: Expedition about $1,995 CAD, McMurdo about $500 CAD, Marquam Peak about $450 CAD. Retailer offers differ by model variant, size and sale.

Pros and cons in brief: Expedition — warmest in its class, long coverage, made in Canada; cons: near $2,000 retail, bulky for everyday city use. Therme — weather protection plus insulation, cleaner urban silhouette, hybrid fill handles damp spots; cons: price varies widely by retailer and variant, not warmest for extreme standing cold. McMurdo — mid price, long coverage, protective hood; cons: needs a warm base layer for long inactive time at −30°C. Marquam Peak Fusion II — lowest price on the page, hooded longer cut, easy-care synthetic fill; cons: synthetic fill is less warm per weight than down, not built for extreme exposure.

## How We Pick — Methodology

What we do: start from published specifications; read professional reviews and user reviews, good and bad; compare by job, not by one winner; check real retailer listings with checked dates; state the limits (brand ratings are brand claims). What we do not do: no hands-on testing claims and no test scores; no fake reviewers (the site has no named reviewer persona); no copied content (no retailer photos, descriptions, or scraped listings); no guessed links or prices; no fake certainty — where sources disagree, the page says so. Picks are labelled best for and not best for, with pros and cons. If a better-documented option appears, the pick changes and the page date changes with it. If a price, specification or link is wrong, or if any retailer or brand asks for a listing to be removed, it is corrected or removed.
